access and updates. The following 4-digit account numbers need to be inserted into the AVL tree in
this order: 1420, 1300, 1250, 1310, 1500, 1550, 1530.
i) Insert the account numbers one by one into the AVL tree, performing rotations whenever the tree
becomes unbalanced.
ii) After all insertions, delete the account numbers 1530 and 1420 from the tree, rebalancing as
necessary.
At each step (after every insertion and deletion), show the balance factor of each node.
reason: Hand-trace AVL insertion of seven given keys, then two deletions, showing rotations and balance factors. The keys and operations are supplied, so this is a trace with no implementation. It is long but stays Easy. The catalog has no AVL match, and #108 does not maintain AVL balance.

Write a function to convert an infix expression to postfix. Include the following functions as per the
prototype.

ii) int IncomingPrecedence(char op); to return the precedence of the incoming operator.
iii) void Infix_Postfix(char infix[], char postfix[]); to convert given infix expression to postfix.
Main function not required.
Note: The infix expression may include ONLY the following operators (listed in the order of their
precedence):
• ^ (exponentiation) → right associative
• * (multiplication), / (division) → left associative
• + (addition), - (subtraction) → left associative
reason: Implement stack-based infix-to-postfix conversion. The in-stack and incoming precedence functions must handle right-associative ^ correctly alongside the left-associative operators. Precedence and associativity cases make it Medium. #150 evaluates postfix and does not convert infix, so it is not a match.

reason: Write doubly linked list insertion at the tail, deletion at the head, and display, which together act as a queue. Each is a familiar operation; the only extra care is updating prev and next pointers and handling the empty list. #707 is a partial match when solved with a doubly linked representation.

text:
An AVL Tree is created by inserting the following keys in Chronological order:
O, G, T, E, L, Y, Z.
After successful insertion, the key G is deleted.

i. The structure of the AVL tree before and after deletion.
ii. Identify the type of imbalance.Specify the rotation(s) used to restore balance.
reason: Hand-trace of AVL insertion then deletion on supplied keys. Inserting Z causes an RR imbalance at T, fixed by a single left rotation, which gives O(G(E,L), Y(T,Z)). Deleting G (replaced by its inorder successor L or predecessor E) leaves the tree balanced. Pure trace, so Easy. No catalog problem covers AVL maintenance.

text:
A small delivery network is represented as an undirected graph. The network has six hubs labelled
A, B, C, D, E, F. The direct connections between hubs are: A-B, A-C, B-D, C-E, D-F, E-F, B-C, D-E
Note: Whenever there is a choice between multiple unvisited neighbours in DFS or BFS, hubs
should be selected in alphabetical order.
i. If a delivery inspection follows Depth First Search (DFS) starting from hub A, which hub will be
inspected last? Explain your reasoning.
ii. If a delivery inspection follows Breadth First Search (BFS) starting from hub A, which hub is the
farthest from A in terms of the number of connections?
iii. Determine the number of connected subnetworks in this network.
Now, remove the link E-F and D-F from the network. How many connected subnetworks exist after
these removals?
iv. If all connections become one-way (directed) in the order: A→ B→ D→F, A→C→E→F, B→C,
D→ E, can DFS starting from A reach all hubs? Provide a brief explanation.
v. Which change in the underlying data structure (queue ↔ stack) would make BFS behave like

DFS?
reason: Several short traces on a 6-vertex graph: DFS order (A,B,C,E,D,F, so F is last), BFS distance (F farthest at 3 edges), component count (1, and still 1 after removals with F isolated? No: removing E-F and D-F isolates F, giving 2), directed reachability (yes), and the queue-to-stack swap. DFS is the first substantive task; BFS, components and reachability are secondary. Pure hand simulation. #547 and #1971 implement these ideas but are not needed for a trace.
